observations.seen: Frame 1 is lit like an overcast midday: a grey-blue sky, a flat grey road and no low warm key, so the golden-hour recipe is missing. Frame 3 is the only warm frame, and its canyon walls are lit almost uniformly with no rim or raking light. In the night frame the streetlights cast no light pools and the tower windows do not glow.

Trees on the coastal hillside cast readable shadows. The car's ground shadow in frame 2 shows blocky, checkered shadow-map aliasing under the rear wheels. In frames 3 and 4 the contact shadow under the car is faint and soft, so the car looks lightly detached from the road.

The teal paint has broad specular highlights and the roll bars read as metal, but the body does not reflect the sky or the canyon. The sea in frames 1 and 2 is drawn as horizontal stripe bands with no sky reflection. The night road has a faint moonlit sheen, the strongest reflection cue in the set.

The coast has wind turbines, low-poly trees, orange rock clusters and red-roof houses on a flat yellow hill with no detail on its surface. The canyon walls are large planar slabs with stripe banding. The night city is plain boxes with striped window textures and almost no props near the road.

Distance fog is present in every frame and gives depth to the canyon and the night horizon. In frame 1 the haze is so heavy that it washes out the midground and sky contrast, and the far hills fade to the same grey as the sky.

The asphalt has a convincing grainy aggregate texture. The terrain, canyon rock and building facades are flat colour or simple banding without roughness or normal variation. The gate signs ('HARBOUR RELAY') render as blurry, aliased pixel text.

The roadster is the most detailed asset, with roll hoops, a cockpit interior and racing stripes. The traffic vehicles, trees, rocks and towers are much lower fidelity, so the scene mixes detail levels.

The car takes up roughly 14–20% of the frame width but a small share of the frame area, below the recipe's 15–25% subject target. Frames 3 and 4 offset the car to the right with good road leading lines. Frame 1 centres the car and fills the upper half with empty grey sky.

A chase camera with an apparent FOV of about 60–65°. The lateral offset in frames 3 and 4 suggests camera lag or drift framing. The low camera height works, but frame 1 shows no speed cues such as FOV kick or motion blur at 217 km/h.

Frame 1 has low contrast and lifted blacks. Frame 3 has a purple-orange grade with vignette, and frame 4 has a blue grade with mild bloom on the moon. None of the frames reaches the recipe's cinematic-film look: there is no filmic tone curve, grain or halation, and the night windows do not bloom.

The HUD is clean and legible: a timer, relay count, segmented progress bar, a speedometer arc at 217 km/h, thrust and heat bars, and a combo badge. The 'CLEAN LANDING' toast overlaps the gate sign and is hard to read against the hazy sky. The menu panel is readable and well spaced.

nextChange.change: raise shadow strength toward the look target and pull the key light to an angle that throws visible contact shadows
